name: [D1] Commit complete batch and capability lifecycle state (M)
description:
Commit complete batch and capability lifecycle state

Location: src/ovcaq/state/commands.py; src/ovcaq/runtime/supervisor.py; tests/state/test_supervisor_commands.py; tests/runtime/test_supervisor.py; tests/runtime/test_capability_lifecycle.py; tests/packaging/test_installed_supervisor_cli.py

Reuse: existing StateStore/StateService, pure decisions, shared runtime ownership and test fixtures.

Contract (source requirement/design excerpts):
Failure sets attempt/capability `failed`,
`batch.status="attention"`, and `control.attention` in one transaction without
changing `work`, `tasks`, `review`, or `batch.completed_prds`.
Success sets attempt/capability `succeeded`; when every required capability succeeded it
sets `batch.status="completed"`, `batch.completed_at`, and clears capability
attention.

Details:
Repair shared mutable batch state only through guarded StateService/StateStore transactions. Under the existing run lock, initialize an unstarted batch with a unique nonblank id, running status and injected started_at before publishing its first metric; preserve an already-started batch and all workflow-owned subtrees. Prove installed init -> run launches without a test-only batch SEED. Capability failure must set batch.status=attention. Success clears only attention belonging to the successful capability, never unrelated attention. Before terminal archive commit completed status and injected completed_at even when no required capabilities exist. Empty-drain completion must use injected time. Preserve required pending/running/failed guards, pins, attempt evidence, and drained PRD results. No state schema migration or new public CLI verb is needed.

### Findings (verbatim)
- 🟠 Capability failure leaves `batch.status` as running, and a later successful retry does not clear its stale `control.attention`, violating the lifecycle contract and leaving completed state with failure attention | File: src/ovcaq/state/commands.py:554 | Consensus: [3/3]
- 🟠 No production code ever starts a batch. Nothing in `src/` writes `batch.id` or `batch.status="running"`, and `new_state` leaves `batch.id=""`. So `ovcaq init` followed by `ovcaq run --no-tui` raises at `_open_session` → `publish_session_metric` → `_validate_identifier("")`, and `archive_final_state` also requires the id. The installed drain acceptance test passes only because its SEED script writes the batch fields straight through StateStore | File: tests/packaging/test_installed_supervisor_cli.py:68 | Consensus: [1/3]
- 🟡 The batch status lifecycle is incomplete. `apply(COMPLETE)` only archives, so a drain with no *required* capability (non-empty drain, or empty drain with only optional pending capabilities) archives `batch.status` still `running`. A failed capability never sets `batch.status="attention"`, which plan §8.6 step 5 requires | File: src/ovcaq/runtime/supervisor.py:236 | Consensus: [1/3]
- ⚪ `skip_empty_drain_capabilities` stamps `completed_at` from `datetime.now(UTC)` instead of the injected clock, unlike `finish_capability` (PRD: injectable time) | File: src/ovcaq/state/commands.py:601 | Consensus: [1/3]

Acceptance criteria:
- Every quoted finding no longer reproduces.
- Every decision is explainable from committed state plus summary.
- Metrics, pause, stop, retry, park, and halt contracts pass.
- Required post-drain capability lifecycle and independent retry pass.

Verify: tests fail for the quoted regression before implementation and pass after; run applicable focused tests, source quality gates, and the work skill's mandatory final verification. Do not read live launcher homes in tests.
